tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

{"issues":{"nodes":[{"expand":"renderedFields,names,schema,operations,editmeta,changelog,versionedRepresentations","id":"18439","key":"SW-600","fields":{"summary":"SW-589 W7: Training, threshold and tuning","issuetype":{"id":"10003","description":"Subtasks track small pieces of work that are part of a larger task.","iconUrl":"https://jira-prod-eu-13-2.prod.atl-paas.net/rest/api/2/universal_avatar/view/type/issuetype/avatar/10316?size=medium","name":"Subtask","subtask":true,"avatarId":10316,"entityId":"498cec2b-1a84-46f0-9566-43c224c66104","hierarchyLevel":-1},"components":[],"created":"2026-11-19T08:05:05.495+0200","description":"**Goal:** make sure training runs per trace, the threshold is fitted on patient-grouped folds, and tuning doesn't reward loosening the clinical floors.

**Scope:** 6 findings and 1 question for the author:

* 4 to fix: G6, M12, M13, L15.

"""SW-589 L5, L6: ThresholdClassifier must not fall back to 0.5 silently."""
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

from src.core.train import ThresholdClassifier


def _separable(n_per_class=12, rows_per_patient=1):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    X = np.vstack([rng.normal(-2, 1, (n_per_class, 2)), rng.normal(2, 1, (n_per_class, 2))])
    y = np.array([0] * n_per_class + [1] * n_per_class)
    groups = np.arange(len(y)) // rows_per_patient
    return X, y, groups


def test_constraints_nobody_can_meet_warn_and_flag_the_fallback():
    """L5: if no threshold meets min_sensitivity/min_specificity, 0.5 used to be kept silently."""
    X, y, groups = _separable()
    # Labels that can't be learned: no threshold reaches 100% sens and 100% spec.
    y = np.tile([0, 1], len(y) // 2)
    clf = ThresholdClassifier(LogisticRegression(), cv_folds=3, min_sensitivity=1.0, min_specificity=1.0)

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="min_sensitivity"):
        clf.fit(X, y, groups)

    assert clf.threshold_ == 0.5
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_ is True
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_reason_ == "constraints_unmet"


def test_single_class_training_set_warns_and_flags_the_fallback():
    """L6: a training set with one class used to set 0.5 silently and leave the flag unset."""
    X, y, groups = _separable()
    y = np.zeros_like(y)
    clf = ThresholdClassifier(LogisticRegression(), cv_folds=3)

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="one class"):
        clf.fit(X, y, groups)

    assert clf.threshold_ == 0.5
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_ is True
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_reason_ == "single_class"


def test_too_few_patients_per_class_warns_and_flags_the_fallback():
    """L6: a class with fewer than 2 patients can't be cross-validated; 0.5 used to be set silently."""
    X, y, groups = _separable(n_per_class=4, rows_per_patient=4)
    clf = ThresholdClassifier(LogisticRegression(), cv_folds=3)

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="fewer than 2 patients"):
        clf.fit(X, y, groups)

    assert clf.threshold_ == 0.5
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_ is True
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_reason_ == "too_few_patients"


def test_normal_fit_does_not_warn_and_is_not_a_fallback():
    X, y, groups = _separable()
    clf = ThresholdClassifier(LogisticRegression(), cv_folds=3)

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)
        clf.fit(X, y, groups)

    assert clf.threshold_fallback_ is False
    assert clf.threshold_fallback_reason_ is None

"""SW-589 M1, H6: the threshold is chosen on patient-grouped folds.

M1: ``ThresholdClassifier`` tuned its threshold on out-of-fold scores from
row-level folds, so a patient's other rows (fwts, device channels) could sit in
the fold's training part. 1bfe9ba switched it to ``StratifiedGroupKFold`` on
patient ids; this pins it.
"""

import numpy as np
import pytest
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

from src.core.train import ThresholdClassifier

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit


class SpyLogisticRegression(LogisticRegression):
    """Records the patients (column 0) each inner fit trains and predicts on."""

    calls: list[tuple[str, frozenset]] = []

    def fit(self, X, y, sample_weight=None):
        SpyLogisticRegression.calls.append(("fit", frozenset(np.asarray(X)[:, 0])))
        return super().fit(np.asarray(X)[:, 1:], y, sample_weight)

    def predict_proba(self, X):
        SpyLogisticRegression.calls.append(("predict", frozenset(np.asarray(X)[:, 0])))
        return super().predict_proba(np.asarray(X)[:, 1:])


def _many_rows_per_patient(n_patients=20, rows_per_patient=6, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    patients = np.repeat(np.arange(n_patients), rows_per_patient)
    y = (patients % 2).astype(int)
    features = rng.normal(y[:, None] * 1.5, 1.0, (len(y), 2))
    X = np.column_stack([patients.astype(float), features])
    return X, y, patients


def test_no_patient_is_on_both_sides_of_a_threshold_fold():
    SpyLogisticRegression.calls = []
    X, y, patients = _many_rows_per_patient()

    ThresholdClassifier(SpyLogisticRegression(), cv_folds=5).fit(X, y, patients)

    inner = SpyLogisticRegression.calls[:-1]  # the last call is the final full fit
    folds = list(zip(inner[0::2], inner[1::2]))
    assert len(folds) == 5
    for (fit_call, fit_patients), (predict_call, predict_patients) in folds:
        assert (fit_call, predict_call) == ("fit", "predict")
        assert not fit_patients & predict_patients
    every_validated = set().union(*(p for (_, _), (_, p) in folds))
    assert every_validated == set(patients.astype(float))

from src.core.train import ThresholdClassifier

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit


class SpyLogisticRegression(LogisticRegression):
    """Records the patients (column 0) each inner fit trains and predicts on."""

    calls: list[tuple[str, frozenset]] = []

    def fit(self, X, y, sample_weight=None):
        SpyLogisticRegression.calls.append(("fit", frozenset(np.asarray(X)[:, 0])))
        return super().fit(np.asarray(X)[:, 1:], y, sample_weight)

    def predict_proba(self, X):
        SpyLogisticRegression.calls.append(("predict", frozenset(np.asarray(X)[:, 0])))
        return super().predict_proba(np.asarray(X)[:, 1:])


def _many_rows_per_patient(n_patients=20, rows_per_patient=6, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    patients = np.repeat(np.arange(n_patients), rows_per_patient)
    y = (patients % 2).astype(int)
    features = rng.normal(y[:, None] * 1.5, 1.0, (len(y), 2))
    X = np.column_stack([patients.astype(float), features])
    return X, y, patients


def test_no_patient_is_on_both_sides_of_a_threshold_fold():
    SpyLogisticRegression.calls = []
    X, y, patients = _many_rows_per_patient()

    ThresholdClassifier(SpyLogisticRegression(), cv_folds=5).fit(X, y, patients)

    inner = SpyLogisticRegression.calls[:-1]  # the last call is the final full fit
    folds = list(zip(inner[0::2], inner[1::2]))
    assert len(folds) == 5
    for (fit_call, fit_patients), (predict_call, predict_patients) in folds:
        assert (fit_call, predict_call) == ("fit", "predict")
        assert not fit_patients & predict_patients
    every_validated = set().union(*(p for (_, _), (_, p) in folds))
    assert every_validated == set(patients.astype(float))

    traces = result["trace_level_statistics"]

class FitRecorder(LogisticRegression):

def evaluate_easy_ensemble_trial(
    trial: optuna.Trial,
    tuning_input: FeatureTuningInput,
    folds: Sequence[tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]],
    *,
    random_seed: int,
    threshold_config: Mapping[str, Any],
    search_space: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
    fixed_parameters: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> float:
    """Evaluate one Easy Ensemble parameter set with the production threshold wrapper."""
    data = tuning_input.data
    X = data.loc[:, tuning_input.feature_columns].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    y = _positive_label_mask(data, tuning_input).astype(int).to_numpy()
    patient_groups = data[tuning_input.patient_column].astype(str).to_numpy()
    parameters = {
        **_suggest_balanced_rf_parameters(trial, search_space),
        **fixed_parameters,
    }
    resolved_threshold = resolve_trial_threshold_config(trial, threshold_config)
    fold_metrics: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    for fold_number, (train_indices, validation_indices) in enumerate(folds):
        try:
            model = _fit_patient_aware_threshold_model(
                EasyEnsembleClassifier(**parameters),
                X[train_indices],
                y[train_indices],
                patient_groups[train_indices],
                threshold_config=resolved_threshold,
            )
            metrics = _fold_metrics(
                y[validation_indices], model.predict(X[validation_indices])
            )
        except ValueError:
            metrics = {
                "sensitivity": 0.0,
                "specificity": 0.0,
                "balanced_accuracy": 0.0,
            }
        fold_metrics.append(metrics)
        trial.report(
            float(np.mean([value["balanced_accuracy"] for value in fold_metrics])),
            step=fold_number,
        )

    for metric_name in ("balanced_accuracy", "sensitivity", "specificity"):
        values = [metrics[metric_name] for metrics in fold_metrics]
        trial.set_user_attr(f"mean_{metric_name}", float(np.mean(values)))
        trial.set_user_attr(f"std_{metric_name}", float(np.std(values)))
    return float(np.mean([metrics["balanced_accuracy"] for metrics in fold_metrics]))

    feature_run_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    output_name: str,
    config_path: str | Path,
) -> Path:
    """Run or resume an XGBoost study and write a model-catalog-compatible result."""

"""SW-589 L15: tuning runs that can be trusted and repeated.

- EasyEnsemble scored a fold that raised ValueError as 0, which steered the
  search away from those settings as if they were bad. Such a trial now fails
  (pruned) with the reason recorded.
- A study resumed with ``load_if_exists`` even when the tuning config or the
  feature run had changed, mixing incomparable trials. Resuming now checks a
  fingerprint and refuses a mismatch.
- The summary says whether the run is reproducible (``parallel_trials`` 1).
"""

import json
import warnings

import optuna
import pytest
import yaml

import src.core.easy_ensemble_tuning as ee
from src.core.easy_ensemble_tuning import run_easy_ensemble_tuning
from tests.unit.test_easy_ensemble_tuning import _write_feature_run, _write_tuning_config

pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit


def test_a_failing_fold_fails_the_trial_instead_of_scoring_zero(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    def broken(*args, **kwargs):
        raise ValueError("Not enough samples of the minority class")

    monkeypatch.setattr(ee, "_fit_patient_aware_threshold_model", broken)
    feature_run = _write_feature_run(tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="No trials are completed"):
        run_easy_ensemble_tuning(
            feature_run, output_name="broken", config_path=_write_tuning_config(tmp_path)
        )
    storage = feature_run / "hyperparameter_tuning" / "broken" / "study.sqlite3"
    study = optuna.load_study(study_name="broken", storage=f"sqlite:///{storage}")
    assert all(t.state == optuna.trial.TrialState.PRUNED for t in study.trials)
    assert "minority class" in study.trials[0].user_attrs["failed_fold"]


def test_resuming_with_a_different_config_is_refused(tmp_path):
    feature_run = _write_feature_run(tmp_path)
    config_path = _write_tuning_config(tmp_path)
    run_easy_ensemble_tuning(feature_run, output_name="study", config_path=config_path)

    config = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    config["tuning"]["n_trials"] = 3
    config["search_space"]["n_estimators"]["high"] = 3
    config_path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config), encoding="utf-8")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="different tuning config or feature run"):
        run_easy_ensemble_tuning(feature_run, output_name="study", config_path=config_path)


def test_summary_records_whether_the_run_is_reproducible(tmp_path):
    feature_run = _write_feature_run(tmp_path)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        output = run_easy_ensemble_tuning(
            feature_run, output_name="study", config_path=_write_tuning_config(tmp_path)
        )
    summary_path = next(output.parent.glob("*summary*.json"))
    summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert summary["parallel_trials"] == 1
    assert summary["reproducible"] is True

|---|---|---|

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |

| L15 | 3 | `test_tuning_robustness.py` | failing fold prunes the trial (reason recorded, clear error when none completes); resume with a changed config refused; summary records `parallel_trials` and `reproducible` | All 3 red |
| **Total** | **9** | | | 6 red; G6's 3 are a verification |

**Full suite:** see below.

## Metric comparison
Not needed for group A: no shipped model, default config or training path changes. Tuning results can differ from before (H6: thresholds follow production's fold seed), but no model was re-tuned.

- **M12 + L15 youden (Gilad):** stop searching the clinical floors and the threshold metric in the tuning configs.
- **M13 (Gilad, Eran):** repeated patient CV, 1-SE rule, patient-level objective.
- **L15 xgboost pin (Avichai):** one version in every requirements file (2.1.1 suggested: lock file and current venv).

SW-603 (in PR #52), SW-604, SW-605 (planned for W8), SW-611 (with SW-606): none in W7 scope, not touched.

```bash
git log --oneline sw589-W7-start..sw589-W7A-review

git diff docs/pipeline_review_findings.md   # uncommitted findings text
```

message.content: Elaborate on item M12 and L15. Give me the context briefly, what you fixed and what is opening?

content.text:
## Context: how tuning works
Tuning tries hundreds of model settings (about 800 trials) to find the best ones. For each trial it trains a model and then chooses a **decision threshold**: the probability above which a patient is called LC. Two kinds of setting control that threshold choice:
- **Clinical floors:** `min_sensitivity` and `min_specificity`. A threshold is only allowed if it reaches at least, say, 70% sensitivity and 65% specificity.
- **Threshold metric:** which score to maximise among the allowed thresholds, `balanced_accuracy` or `youden`.

Each trial is then scored by its balanced accuracy, and the best-scoring trial wins.

## M12: tuning searches the clinical floors (nothing fixed yet)
**Issue:** the tuning configs let the search **change the floors themselves**, for example sensitivity anywhere from 0.65 to 0.80 and specificity from 0.55 to 0.70. Since the winner is the trial with the best balanced accuracy, the search learns that lower floors give more freedom, so it drifts towards the **loosest floors it's allowed**. The review saw this: the shipped XGBoost sits exactly at the lower bounds, 0.65 / 0.55.

**Why it matters:** the floors are meant to be fixed clinical requirements, not something to optimise. Searching them trades clinical safety for a better-looking score.

**Open, needs Gilad:** fix the floors at the clinical values in each tuning config and stop searching them. That's a config-only change, and no shipped model changes until someone re-tunes. The question is which floor values to use.

## L15: tuning reproducibility and hygiene (4 parts, 3 fixed)

| Part | Issue | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **a. Failed folds scored 0** | When EasyEnsemble couldn't fit a fold (`ValueError`), the trial scored 0 for that fold. The search then avoided those settings as if they were bad, though they had only failed to run | **Fixed:** the trial now fails (pruned), with the reason recorded. If no trial completes, the run stops with a clear message |
| **b. Resume and parallel runs** | A study always resumed an existing study of the same name, even after the config or the feature data had changed, mixing trials that can't be compared. Running 4 trials in parallel also makes the result depend on timing, so the same seed doesn't give the same study | **Fixed:** resuming checks a fingerprint of the config and data and refuses a mismatch. The summary records `parallel_trials` and whether the run is reproducible (only with 1), with a warning otherwise |
| **c. youden = balanced accuracy** | Youden equals 2 × balanced accuracy − 1, so both always pick the same threshold. Searching between them wastes trials | **Open (Gilad):** drop it from the search, in the same config edit as M12 |
| **d. xgboost versions differ** | Three requirements files pin different xgboost versions: 3.0.2, 2.1.1 and ≥1.6.0. The Windows venv runs 2.1.1 | **Open (Avichai):** choose one version for all files. I'd suggest 2.1.1 (the lock file and the current venv) unless he wants 3.0.2 |

So: **M12 is all open**, waiting for Gilad's floor values. **L15 is three-quarters done.** Its two open parts are small edits once Gilad (youden) and Avichai (xgboost) answer.

message.content: Elaborate on item M13. Give me the context briefly, what you fixed and what is opening?

content.text:
**M13: nothing fixed yet. The whole item is open and needs Gilad and Eran.**

## Context
Tuning tries about 800 combinations of model settings, scores each one, and keeps the best. M13 is about **how that best one is chosen**. The review points to three weaknesses.

## The issue

**1. One fixed split for every trial**
Every trial is scored on the same 5 cross-validation folds (one patient split). With so few patients per fold, a trial's score depends partly on luck: which patients happened to land in which fold.

**2. "Pick the top score" rewards that luck (the winner's curse)**
Among 800 trials, the top one is usually the one that both works well **and** got lucky with that particular split. So its score overstates how good it really is, and it may not be the best choice on new patients.

Example: 50 trials are truly about equally good, at around 0.70 balanced accuracy. Fold luck spreads their scores between 0.66 and 0.75. Picking the top trial chooses the luckiest one, reported at 0.75 although it's really about 0.70.

**3. The score counts rows, not patients**
Each fold's balanced accuracy is computed per row (trace or exam). Patients with many rows count more, while the pipeline's reported results are per patient.

The finding also notes the data was "selection-leaked": features were chosen on the whole pool before tuning. The tuning summary already says its scores "are not an independent final generalization estimate", so that part is documented rather than fixed.

## What's open (my recommendation)

| Change | What it does | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Repeated CV** (e.g. 3 different 5-fold splits) | Averages out fold luck | About 3× the tuning time |
| **1-SE rule** | Among trials within one standard error of the best, take the simplest (e.g. fewer or shallower trees) instead of the top score | Little: it uses the scores already computed |
| **Patient-level balanced accuracy** | Scores each fold per patient, matching how results are reported | Little |

All three only change **how tuning picks settings**. No shipped model changes until someone re-tunes.

**Questions for Gilad and Eran:**
1. Is ~3× tuning time acceptable for repeated CV, and how many repeats?
2. Use the 1-SE rule? It needs a definition of "simplest" per model (for example fewer trees or less depth).
3. Switch the trial score to patient-level balanced accuracy?

# Review: SW-589 W7, training, threshold and tuning

- **Status:** group A `[r]` awaiting Tram's review · group B waiting for decisions · **Jira:** SW-600 (In Progress)
- **Branch:** `tram/sw-589-training-defaults` (PR 3: W6, W7, G3, G9)
- **Range (group A):** `sw589-W7-start..sw589-W7A-review` (4 commits)
- **Not committed yet:** the group A text in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`.

## Group A: scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | ACCEPTED (fix in 1bfe9ba) | **FIXED** | Regression test added. Note: 1bfe9ba already came with two tests for it (fit side); the new test adds the validation side |
| H6 | ACCEPTED (fix in 1bfe9ba) | **FIXED** | Tuning now calls the production `ThresholdClassifier.fit` instead of its own copy |
| Q4 | open | **answered** | Yes: patient-grouped folds in production (1bfe9ba) and in tuning (H6) |
| G6 | ACCEPTED (waiting for Eran) | **FIXED** (verified) | Test proves per-trace training fits on traces; no code change. Eran's confirmation on a real run still welcome |
| L15 | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED, **3 fixes** | Failing EasyEnsemble folds fail the trial; resume guard; reproducibility recorded. Youden search and xgboost pin wait for group B |

## Commits

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 9415cf3 | M1 | Add a regression test for patient-grouped threshold folds |
| c65e01f | H6 | Choose tuning thresholds with the production ThresholdClassifier |
| 1c18823 | G6 | Verify that per-trace training fits on traces |
| 3d5c7e1 | L15 | Fail unfittable tuning trials, guard study resume, record reproducibility |
| (uncommitted) | M1, H6, Q4, G6, L15 | Findings text |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/balanced_rf_tuning.py`** (H6, L15): `_fit_patient_aware_threshold_model` now builds a `ThresholdClassifier` from the trial's threshold settings (including `min_pos_rate`) and calls its `fit`. New shared helpers: `open_tuning_study` (fingerprint check), `reproducibility_record`, `require_completed_trial`.
2. **`src/core/easy_ensemble_tuning.py`** (L15): a fold raising `ValueError` prunes the trial (`failed_fold` recorded) instead of scoring 0.
3. **`src/core/xgboost_tuning.py`** (H6, L15): same helpers.
4. **Tests:** 4 new files.

Only tuning outputs can change. Training, shipped model YAMLs and default configs are untouched.

## Test evidence

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | 1 | `test_threshold_patient_folds.py` | 20 patients x 6 rows, 5 inner folds: no patient on both the fit and the validation side of a fold; every patient validated once | Fails on `train.py` before 1bfe9ba (temporary worktree): with the old `fit(X, y)` 13 to 18 of 20 patients were on both sides of each fold |
| H6 | 2 | `test_threshold_patient_folds.py` | tuning's threshold, fall-back flag and `min_pos_rate` equal production's (`min_pos_rate` 0 and 0.45) | Both red. Before, tuning seeded its folds with `random_seed + fold`: thresholds 0.6182 / 0.4772 vs training's 0.5493 in 4 of 5 outer folds |
| G6 | 3 | `test_training_fits_on_traces.py` | final fit of each permutation sees every training trace (3 per exam); a patient never in two splits per permutation; patient stats = exam votes (mean channel probability) aggregated | Pass before and after: a verification, nothing to fix |
| L15 | 3 | `test_tuning_robustness.py` | failing fold prunes the trial (reason recorded, clear error when none completes); resume with a changed config refused; summary records `parallel_trials` and `reproducible` | All 3 red |
| **Total** | **9** | | | 6 red; G6's 3 are a verification |

**Full suite** (both runs on 2026-11-25):

| | Passed | Failed | xfailed | Collection errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W7 start (`sw589-W7-start`) | 548 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| W7 group A | **557** (+9) | 3 (same) | 6 (same) | 1 (same) |

The 3 failures and the collection error are the known ones (SW-611, the Windows symlink test, the visualization test, SW-610).

## Metric comparison
Not needed for group A: no shipped model, default config or training path changes. Tuning results can differ from before (H6: thresholds follow production's fold seed), but no model was re-tuned.

## Decisions I made (please check)
1. **M1:** kept the new test although 1bfe9ba already has two. Theirs check the fit side only; the new one checks the validation side and that every patient is validated.
2. **H6:** tuning follows production's fixed fold seed (42) instead of `random_seed + fold`. The `random_seed` argument of the trial functions is now unused; I kept it so callers don't break.
3. **G6:** marked FIXED as "verified" with the test as proof, and noted that Eran's confirmation on a real per-trace run is still welcome.
4. **L15:** a failing EasyEnsemble fold prunes the whole trial (not just that fold), since a partial mean would compare trials on different folds.
5. **L15:** a study without a recorded fingerprint (made before this change) still resumes, with a warning, and gets the fingerprint from then on.
6. **L15:** parallel runs are allowed but flagged as not reproducible; the default stays `parallel_trials: 4`.

## Group B (waiting)
- **M12 + L15 youden (Gilad):** stop searching the clinical floors and the threshold metric in the tuning configs.
- **M13 (Gilad, Eran):** repeated patient CV, 1-SE rule, patient-level objective.
- **L15 xgboost pin (Avichai):** one version in every requirements file (2.1.1 suggested: lock file and current venv).

## Bug tickets
SW-603 (in PR #52), SW-604, SW-605 (planned for W8), SW-611 (with SW-606): none in W7 scope, not touched.

## How to review
```bash
git log --oneline sw589-W7-start..sw589-W7A-review
git diff sw589-W7-start..sw589-W7A-review -- src/core/balanced_rf_tuning.py src/core/easy_ensemble_tuning.py
git diff docs/pipeline_review_findings.md   # uncommitted findings text
```

- **Status:** group A `[x]` approved by Tram on 2026-11-22 · group B waiting for decisions · **Jira:** SW-598 (In Progress)
- **Branch:** `tram/sw-589-preprocess-features` (same as W4; PR 2)
- **Range (group A):** `sw589-W5-start..sw589-W5A-review` (3 commits)
- **Findings text:** committed after approval.

## Group A: scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| G7 | FIXED (test open) | **FIXED**, with test | Regression test: filtered rows go to the estimation set |
| M3 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Stability uses the run's selection settings; method failures are reported |
| L14 | ACCEPTED | ACCEPTED, **3 bugs fixed** | Median fill, quota size, unknown settings rejected. MI on bootstrap duplicates stays for group B |

## Commits

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 1854dfa | G7 | Add a regression test for filtered rows in the estimation set |
| f376997 | M3 | Measure stability with the run's selector settings and report failures |
| 4abb5ea | L14 | Fix the poolsel median fill and quota size, reject unknown settings |
| (uncommitted) | G7, M3, L14 | Findings text |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/feature_selection_poolsel.py`** (L14): the v1 redundancy step reads raw columns so the median rule runs; the quota pass stops at the pool size. Affects only `patient_mrmr_consensus` runs (relive_beta, type1_61, lucia550 mrmr_sites).
2. **`src/core/config/validate.py`** (L14): `patient_mrmr_consensus` settings checked against what the funnel accepts, for `features` and `holdout.selection`.
3. **`src/core/feature_stability.py`, `src/core/stages/features.py`** (M3): stability gets `selection_kwargs`; failures counted, warned, written and shown.
4. **Tests:** 4 new files.

## Test evidence

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G7 | 1 | `test_estimation_keeps_filtered_rows.py` | other study group, other sensor, other breath and an invalid row go to `estimation_pickle`, none to train/test | Red on the code before 0df6cd8 (only the invalid row reached estimation). Run in a temporary worktree, because the test file's imports changed since |
| M3 | 3 | `test_feature_stability_settings.py` | configured `correlation_threshold` and other settings reach the selector; a method failing in every permutation is warned about, counted, written to the raw JSON and shown in the report; no warning when all succeed | The 2 behaviour cases are red; all 3 fail on the old signature |
| L14 | 7 | `test_poolsel_edge_cases.py` | v1 redundancy step sees the median fill; quota pool capped at its size with 6 sections; unchanged with 4 sections; no scored replicate raises; `correlation_threshold` rejected for poolsel; `holdout.selection` settings checked; valid poolsel settings load | 4 red; the 4-section, no-replicate and valid-settings cases pin behaviour that had to stay |
| **Total** | **11** | | | 7 red |

**Full suite:**

| | Passed | Failed | xfailed | Collection errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| After W4 | 507 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| W5 group A | **518** (+11) | 3 (same) | 6 (same) | 1 (same) |

## Metric comparison
- **Default runs (`ensemble`):** no change. M3 only changes the stability report, which is off by default.
- **`patient_mrmr_consensus` runs:** can change when a TSF column has under 10% missing values (median instead of zero before the redundancy step) or when features come from more than four sections (pool capped at its size). A before/after on a real poolsel run belongs with the group B decisions, which change the same selector.

## Decisions I made (please check)
1. **M3:** stability gives every method the run's `selection_kwargs`, as training does. A method that rejects them now shows up as a reported failure instead of a silent empty result.
2. **M3:** `validate` stays off in stability. It only logs a CV score, so the selection is the same and it saves time.

**Title:** SW-589 (PR 1/5): Review findings triage and safe fixes

**Branch:** `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings` into `master`
**Reviewers:** Gilad, Avichai

## What this PR does
Goes through the PR 38 review findings in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` and lands the fixes that don't change model results. Every finding now has a Resolution line. No model numbers change.

## Findings closed in this PR
| Status | Findings |
|---|---|
| Fixed here (12) | G12, G18, G22, M11, L2, L3, L4, L5, L6, L12, L16, L19 |
| Already fixed on master, confirmed (6) | G1, G4, G5, G7, G13, L9 |
| Won't fix (3) | G2, L1, L13 |
| Waiting (2) | G3 (meeting on 2026-11-23, SW-606), G9 (Eran) |

Each fix has a test that fails on the old code. The other findings come in later PRs.

## Changes reviewers should know about
- Configs whose per-trace settings contradict each other are now rejected before the run starts (G22). All shipped configs still load.
- A holdout run without training now only extracts features and skips the whole-pool selection (G18). Holdout results are identical.
- The removal audit counts visits (G12) and records GRID_CLEAN drops (M11).
- New warnings when the threshold falls back to 0.5 (L5, L6) and when several models are trained (L4).
- Tuning modules import again (SW-603).

## Tests
- 473 passed (386 on master). The 3 failures and 1 collection error also fail on master.
- A system test runs holdout with and without whole-pool selection and checks that all 34 output tables match.

## Found during this work
- SW-603: tuning modules failed to import (fixed here).
- SW-604: model reports from a training run cover only the last model.
- SW-605: `--resume` always reruns the features stage.

## How to review
Start with the Resolution lines in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`. There is one commit per finding, so `git show <hash>` shows one fix and its test. The largest changes are in `src/core/stages/features.py` (G18) and `src/core/config/validate.py` (G22).

# Review: SW-589 W3, config contract and defaults

- **Status:** `[x]` approved by Tram on 2026-11-20 · **Jira:** SW-596 (Done)
- **Branch:** `tram/sw-589-pr38-findings`
- **Range:** `sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review` (5 commits)
- **Goal of W3:** a run's config is checked before it starts, and the defaults are chosen deliberately.
- **Closed early (Tram, 2026-11-19):** G3 and Q1 wait for the 2026-11-23 meeting and G9 waits for Eran, so W3 closes with G22 as its only fix. G3 gets its own commit after the meeting.

## Scope and new statuses

| Finding | Was | Now | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| G22 | ACCEPTED | **FIXED** | Per-trace settings checked when the config loads |
| G9 (+ H2) | ACCEPTED | **WAITING (Eran)** | No per-trace models from Eran on any branch; questions recorded |
| G3 | ACCEPTED | **WAITING (Gilad, Avichai, SW-606)** | Defaults to decide at the 2026-11-23 daily meeting |
| Q1 | open | open, **→ SW-606** | Same meeting as G3 |

1 FIXED; 3 waiting on others, each with an owner.

## Commits

| Hash | Finding | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| 66e81aa | G22 | Check the per-trace config keys when the config is loaded |
| 87446e0 | (all FIXED) | Show only the current state of fixed findings (Tram's rule). Docs only |
| bb69e45 | G9 | Mark as waiting for Eran's per-trace models. Docs only |
| 8fb1b35 | G22 | Explain why null stays true with clustering off. Docs only |
| 2a8ed48 | G3, Q1 | Mark as waiting for the defaults decision (SW-606). Docs only |

## Files changed (riskiest first)

1. **`src/core/config/validate.py`** (G22): new `per_trace_rows`, `resolve_allow_multi_trace`, `_validate_model_report_levels`; called from `validate_pipeline_config`. Replaces the one old check (`unit: trace` + `false`).
2. **`src/core/stages/training.py`** (G22): `training_settings_from_config` uses the shared resolver instead of its own copy of the rule.
3. **`src/core/holdout_estimation.py`** (G22): `prepare_rows` uses the resolver; it read `null` as false before.
4. **`src/core/stages/model_reports.py`** (G22): the missing trace-statistics error names the right setting.
5. **Docs:** `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md` (G22, G9, G3, Q1, and the FIXED-items rewrite).
6. **Tests:** 1 new file, 2 changed.

## Test evidence

**Test cases per finding (30 new cases, 2 changed):**

| Finding | Cases | Test file | What they cover | Red before the change? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G22 | 7 | `test_trace_mode_config.py::test_agreeing_keys_load_and_resolve_the_same_in_training` | every agreeing combination of unit × clustering × flag loads, and training resolves the same value | Pass both times: pins the behaviour that had to stay |
| G22 | 3 | `::test_disagreeing_multi_trace_is_rejected_at_load` | `true` on cluster rows, `false` on `unit: trace`, `false` with clustering off | 2 red (cluster + true, clustering off + false); `unit: trace` + false was already rejected |
| G22 | 4 | `::test_report_levels_that_cannot_be_built_are_rejected_at_load` | patient mixed with cluster; cluster with `source: training`; patient with `source: holdout`; trace on a cluster run | All 4 red (only failed at the report stage before) |
| G22 | 3 | `::test_report_levels_that_can_be_built_load` | auto + patient; holdout + cluster on a cluster run; holdout + trace/cluster on a trace run | Pass both times |
| G22 | 11 | `::test_every_shipped_config_still_loads` | all 11 YAMLs in `configs/pipeline/` and `experiments/` | Pass both times: no shipped config is affected |
| G22 | 1 | `::test_holdout_estimation_resolves_null_like_training` | holdout estimation gets `allow_multi_trace=True` for a per-trace run with `null` | Red (got False) |
| G22 | 1 | `::test_missing_trace_statistics_hint_names_the_real_gate` | the missing-file error mentions `allow_multi_trace` | Red |
| **Total** | **30** | | | **9 red before, all pass now** |

**Changed tests:**
- `test_training_stage.py::test_explicit_multi_trace_setting_overrides_clustering_mode` → `test_multi_trace_on_cluster_rows_is_rejected`. It asserted the mismatch G22 removes; it now expects the rejection (red before the change).
- `test_pipeline_runner.py::test_holdout_model_reports_depend_on_holdout_not_training`: asked for `trace` reports on a cluster run, which G22 rejects. It tests stage planning only, so its levels are now `["cluster"]`.

**Red check method:** `git stash` of `src/` only, run the new tests against the old code, then restore.

**Full suite:**

| | Passed | Failed | xfailed | Collection errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| After W2 | 443 | 3 | 6 | 1 |
| W3 review | **473** (+30) | 3 (same) | 6 (same) | 1 (same) |

- **Invariants:** 18 passed, 6 xfailed (SW-568). No XPASS.
- **System:** 10 passed; the 1 baseline failure (`test_unused_study_group_is_left_out[NOT_LC-L-RAD]`) is unchanged.
- **Synthetic run:** the system tests run the full pipeline through config loading, so every stage now passes the new check. No separate run needed: G22 changes validation only.

## Metric comparison
Not needed. G22 rejects configs that disagree and resolves `null` the same way training already did; every shipped config loads and resolves as before. No model numbers change.

## Decisions made
1. **Clustering off → `null` resolves to true** (confirmed by Tram, documented in G22, 8fb1b35). The finding proposed false; that would make holdout keep one channel per measurement.
2. **`source: auto` keeps its run-time check.** The `holdout` command picks the source only when it runs, so config loading can't know it.
3. **Holdout estimation fixed in G22.** Same rule; it read `null` as false.
4. **W3 closed early** (Tram): G3 and Q1 → SW-606, G9 → Eran.

## Follow-up Jira tickets created
- **SW-606:** decide the default config values (G3, Q1) at the 2026-11-23 daily meeting. Sub-task of SW-589, linked to SW-596.

None open for W3. Waiting on others: G3/Q1 (meeting 2026-11-23), G9 (Eran).

```bash
git log --oneline sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review
git diff --stat sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review
git diff sw589-W3-start..sw589-W3-review -- src/core/config/validate.py   # riskiest
git show 66e81aa                                                          # G22
```

# SW-589 W7: training, threshold and tuning (SW-600)

## Context
W7 is the next workstream of SW-589 (PR 38 review findings). It covers how models are trained, how their decision threshold is chosen, and how hyperparameters are tuned: G6, M1, H6, M12, M13, L15 and question Q4 in `docs/pipeline_review_findings.md`. addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

3. Run a discovered operation with the execute-family tool matching its risk tier: `executeRead({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for read-only lookups, `executeWrite({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for non-destructive creates/updates, `executeDestructive({ name, cloudId, inputs })` for deletes/irreversible changes. Only call with an operation `name` from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

cloudId:
- If YOUR client session has no site context, call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE and reuse the returned cloudId. On any execute-family call, always pass cloudId as a TOP-LEVEL argument (sibling of `name`/`inputs`), never inside `inputs`.

Other context:
- The current user's accountId is available from `atlassianUserInfo`.
- Slim large responses with `responseFields` (dot paths) or a `view` preset (compact/evidence/full).

# Jira custom fields (story points, etc.)
Default view is compact — custom fields are omitted unless you pass view: evidence/full, or fields with this site's customfield_* IDs (IDs differ per site). Values appear under fields.customFields, not as top-level customfield_* keys.

# Recovery protocol
1. On a tool error, retry once with corrected input

Confluence access links: For /wiki/access-link/ URLs, first call resolveConfluenceAccessLink with access_link set to the full URL. Use its returned content ID. Keep the same access_link on EVERY later supported call, including retries, pagination, and comment-type queries. Never probe without the link. Never use the token as an ID or this URL as content_url.

## claude.ai Google Drive
Drive can read the user's files, but it may refuse to move or trash a file that wasn't made through this connector, even one the user owns. Before you move a file with update_file, check the file's canMoveItemWithinDrive capability; before you trash a file with trash_file, check its canTrash capability.
